The intelligence oversight system grew out of the 1970s investigations. It moved from Hughes-Ryan's requirement of a presidential finding for CIA operations abroad to the current rule that the intelligence committees be kept fully and currently informed. After September 11, Congress separated leadership of the intelligence community from leadership of the CIA. Read this unit with the Title 10 and Title 50 page.

## What you should be able to do

- Explain what a covert action finding is and who must receive notice.
- Describe what IRTPA changed about intelligence community leadership.
- Explain how CIPA lets classified cases go to trial.

Read these in order. Each card links to the wiki page and to the official text. Ticking a box saves your progress in this browser only.

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="hughes-ryan-1974"}
[Hughes-Ryan Amendment](../../statutes/hughes-ryan-1974.qmd) [1974]{.reading-year} [Superseded]{.status .status-superseded} [Targeted provision]{.layer-badge}

Section 32 of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1974, which added section 662 to the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/88/1795)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="hughes-ryan-1974"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="intel-oversight-1980"}
[Intel Oversight Act](../../statutes/intel-oversight-1980.qmd) [1980]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Enacted as part of the FY1981 intelligence authorization, it added the oversight title to the National Security Act.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/94/1975), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3091?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="intel-oversight-1980"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="nsa-1947"}
[National Security Act](../../statutes/nsa-1947.qmd) [1947]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The founding charter of the modern national security system. It created the National Security Council and the Central Intelligence Agency, established a separate Air Force, and placed the military departments under a single Secretary of Defense.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/61/495), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3002?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="nsa-1947"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="cia-act-1949"}
[CIA Act](../../statutes/cia-act-1949.qmd) [1949]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Gave the CIA the administrative tools to operate in secret: authority to spend money without the usual accounting rules, to withhold information about its staff and structure, and to procure and transfer funds confidentially.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/63/208), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3501?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="cia-act-1949"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="irtpa-2004"}
[IRTPA](../../statutes/irtpa-2004.qmd) [2004]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Carried out the main recommendations of the 9/11 Commission. It separated leadership of the intelligence community from leadership of the CIA by creating the Director of National Intelligence.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/plaw/108/public/458), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/50/3023?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="irtpa-2004"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="espionage-1917"}
[Espionage Act](../../statutes/espionage-1917.qmd) [1917]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

The principal criminal statute protecting national defense information. It covers classic spying for a foreign power and also the unauthorized retention or disclosure of defense information by people who had lawful access to it.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/40/217), [current code](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/18/793?link-type=html)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="espionage-1917"> I have read this</label>
:::

::: {.reading-card .domain-intelligence data-statute="cipa-1980"}
[CIPA](../../statutes/cipa-1980.qmd) [1980]{.reading-year} [In force]{.status .status-in-force} [Framework statute]{.layer-badge}

Sets pretrial and trial procedures for handling classified information in federal criminal cases, so that a defendant cannot force the government to choose between dropping the case and disclosing secrets.

[Read it: [enacted text](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/94/2025)]{.reading-links} <label class="read-check"><input type="checkbox" data-read="cipa-1980"> I have read this</label>
:::

## Further reading

- [Section 394 (cyber)](../../statutes/sec394-cyber-2018.qmd){.subj}: Affirms the Defense Department's authority to conduct military operations in cyberspace, including clandestine ones and ones short of hostilities, and classifies clandestine military cyber activity as traditional military activity instead of covert action.
- [Section 127e](../../statutes/sec127e-2004.qmd){.subj}: Lets the Secretary of Defense fund foreign forces, irregular forces, groups, or individuals who support or facilitate ongoing U.S. special operations against terrorism.
- [FARA](../../statutes/fara-1938.qmd){.subj}: A disclosure law. People who act in the United States on behalf of foreign governments, parties, or other foreign principals in political or public relations work must register with the Justice Department and report their activities and payments.

## Key terms

**Covert action**
:   Activity to influence conditions abroad where the U.S. role is intended not to be apparent or acknowledged. It requires a written presidential finding and notice to the intelligence committees. Defined at 50 U.S.C. 3093(e).

**Finding**
:   A written presidential determination that a covert action is necessary to support identifiable foreign policy objectives.

**Traditional military activities**
:   The exception that keeps military operations out of the covert action definition, and with it outside the finding process.

## Check yourself

Try to answer each question before opening it.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 1. What did the Hughes-Ryan Amendment require?

That no funds be spent on CIA operations abroad other than intelligence collection unless the President found the operation important to national security and reported it to Congress. It has been superseded. See [Hughes-Ryan Amendment](../../statutes/hughes-ryan-1974.qmd) and [Intel Oversight Act](../../statutes/intel-oversight-1980.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 2. What standard of notice does the oversight title of the National Security Act set?

The executive must keep the two intelligence committees fully and currently informed of intelligence activities, including significant anticipated ones. See [Intel Oversight Act](../../statutes/intel-oversight-1980.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 3. What office did IRTPA create, and why?

The Director of National Intelligence, to separate leadership of the whole intelligence community from leadership of the CIA, as the 9/11 Commission recommended. See [IRTPA](../../statutes/irtpa-2004.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon="false"}
## 4. What problem does CIPA solve?

It sets pretrial and trial procedures for classified information in criminal cases, so a defendant cannot force the government to choose between dropping a case and disclosing secrets. See [CIPA](../../statutes/cipa-1980.qmd).
:::
